messages:
Jin: Quick RFC follow-up — I sketched an approach for adding SLO grace windows combined with a tiny quorum/election for routing changes. Goal: avoid flip-flopping on single-probe spikes. RFC link: https://redwood/rfcs/slo-grace

Alex: Clarify: where does election/quorum live in the policy stack? If two regions disagree on health signals we need deterministic tie-breakers, not random flips.

Maria: My thought: require a small quorum (e.g., 2/3) of regional probes to exceed the threshold before we commit a route change. That prevents one noisy probe from switching the global route.

Sam: 2/3 seems fine but it makes rollout reasoning trickier. Do we have a way to simulate "how many flips would quorum have prevented" over historical telemetry? :thinking:

Jin: Yes — plan is a two-step test: run a simulation against the last 30d of routing telemetry, then a canary (5% traffic) with the new policy. Simulation will produce a false-positive / false-negative summary.

Laura: Ops nit: we need an explicit TTL on quorum decisions so they don't bias routing forever. Suggest a `quorum_ttl: 60s` after which we re-evaluate fresh signals.

Maria: +1 on TTL. Also propose a tenant pin override so critical customers can opt out of grace behavior for immediate failover.

Alex: For determinism, tie-breaker order should be explicit: 1) tenant_pin, 2) region latency delta > threshold, 3) cost_bias. That keeps behavior reproducible.

Sam: Example policy snippet for discussion:
```
policy "slo_grace_election" {
  probe_window: 30s
  latency_threshold_ms: 200
  hold_for: 2s
  quorum: { required_fraction: 0.66, ttl: 60s }
  tie_breaker: ["tenant_pin", "latency_delta", "cost_bias"]
}
```

Jin: Two open tradeoffs I called out in the RFC:
- hold_for vs. tail-latency: longer hold reduces churn but slows reaction to real regressions (risk to SLO).
- quorum size vs. sensitivity: larger quorum increases stability but can delay reaction to real regional failures.

Alex: We should expose these as knobs per deployment tier. Hosted default conservative (hold_for=2s, quorum=0.66). Dedicated can be more aggressive (hold_for=1s, quorum=0.5) but with SLA guardrails and stricter telemetry.

Laura: Ops concern: per-tenant canary telemetry will spike cardinality. We'll need aggregation/bucketing to keep metrics cost reasonable.

Sam: I'll add a simulation job that emits per-tenant rollups and a compact global summary. If metric costs blow up, fallback to sampling or coarse bucketing.

Maria: Action items:
- Maria -> author canary config + rollout playbook (include `quorum_ttl`, `hold_for`, and tie-breakers)
- Sam -> run simulation job against 30d telemetry, produce false-positive report and flip avoidance stats
- Laura -> provide telemetry cost estimate and propose bucketing strategy
- Jin -> update RFC with tiered knobs, deterministic tie-breakers, and explicit rollback/rollback-window guidance

ops-bot: Canary job scheduled: canary/slo-grace-2026-03-22 started (5% traffic)
